description: TL1-005 web/desktop packaging parity registry. One row per Flauz surface capability: the class records the capability's web posture in the current tree, the evidence pins the manifest key / node dependency / node-free subtree that forces the classification, and the recovery path names how a web-blocked surface becomes web-capable without forking core. The gate (build/flauz/scripts/packaging-parity.mjs) re-derives every citation against the live tree and flags DRIFT when the tree moved without a registry update. Report: docs/FLAUZ-PROGRAM/PACKAGING-PARITY.md.

classes.desktop-full: The capability binds to local OS resources or desktop-workbench-only surfaces by design (process spawn, local shell, integrated workbench browser tab). The web product excludes it; the web form, when wanted, is a different provider/executor class, not a degradation of this one.
classes.web-degraded: The capability can serve a web build in a consciously reduced form once unblocked: the forcing module surface is host-agnostic, but part of its backing (state sinks, execution, evidence storage) still rides a desktop-bound seam today. The reduction is documented in the row reason.
classes.web-blocked: The capability cannot ship to a web build under a concrete, removable tree constraint (missing browser entrypoint on the packaging posture row, or a node: import in the current wiring). The constraint is incidental, not architectural: the recovery path removes it without touching src/vs or forking core.
classes.web-full: The capability has zero desktop-only dependencies in its forcing surface: once the owning extension grows a browser entrypoint it runs unchanged in the web extension host.

evidenceKinds.manifest-key: Cites a JSON file (relative to repo root) and a key path (array of segments; segments may contain dots verbatim). The file must parse and the key path must resolve. With 'value' the live value must deep-equal; with 'absent: true' the key path must NOT resolve. Dotted segments are literal key names, never path separators.
evidenceKinds.node-import: Cites a source file that must import the named node: module (static 'from node:...' or dynamic import('node:...')). Proves a node dependency that the web extension host cannot satisfy.
evidenceKinds.node-free: Cites a file or directory under which NO source file (.ts/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs) imports any node: module. Proves the cited surface is host-agnostic.

rows.reason: The overlay rebrands the merged product.json, and the merged file feeds both the desktop build (build/gulpfile.vscode.ts) and the server/web product identity paths. No desktop-only binding; the identity flows to every surface the overlay reaches.
rows.recoveryPath: None needed - the posture is already web-shared through the merged product.json.

rows.capability: default chat agent removal (defaultChatAgent null-deletes the Copilot wiring)
rows.reason: The null-deletes overlay removes the upstream defaultChatAgent key so the Copilot entitlement stack no-ops and the flauz.agent participant resolves as sole default agent. The consumer (chatEntitlementService early-return, chatAgents resolution) lives in the shared workbench layer, not electron-main, so the removal applies identically on web and desktop.
rows.recoveryPath: None needed - host-agnostic by construction.

rows.reason: The product-key grant mechanism is ingested by the shared workbench extension-services layer (extensionsProposedApi.ts), not by a desktop-only host: wherever a granted built-in runs, the grant applies. The per-consumer web posture of each grant is classified on the owning extension's rows below; this row classifies only the mechanism.
rows.recoveryPath: None needed - mechanism is host-agnostic; consumers carry their own rows.

rows.capability: Flauz built-in extension set in the web (server) build
rows.reason: The web build's built-in extension set is filtered by isWebExtension() (build/lib/extensions.ts:351-367): a manifest needs a browser entrypoint (or no main and a web extensionKind) to be web-packaged. All seven flauz-* manifests are main-only today, so a web build of the current tree ships zero Flauz surfaces: nothing desktop-only can silently break the web build because nothing Flauz reaches it - but also nothing Flauz is available on web. Every one of the seven citations below is a tripwire: adding a browser entry to any manifest drifts this row and forces a conscious registry update. (The work order named six extensions; the live tree carries a seventh, flauz-resources from TL3-005 - the gate's glob-driven coverage rule found it, and it is classified like every other surface.)
rows.recoveryPath: Per extension: add a browser entrypoint built from the node-free core each extension already has (see the capability rows), keep desktop-only executors behind the desktop entry, and update this registry in the same commit.

rows.reason: main-only manifest (./dist/extension.js, no browser sibling): upstream isWebExtension() and the runtime extension-kind deduction both classify a main-only manifest as not-web, so the extension is excluded from any web build regardless of its capability classes. The engine floor (^1.140.0) is host-neutral and is NOT the blocker.
rows.recoveryPath: Split the entrypoint: a browser build over the node-free participant/view modules, with the stdio seam client loaded only from the desktop entry (see the seam row).

rows.capability: chat participant surface (flauz.agent default chat agent + Agent Sessions view)
rows.reason: The participant, sessions view and tool modules are node-free and the defaultChatParticipant/chatParticipantAdditions grants are ingested host-agnostically, so the chat surface itself is web-capable. Degraded, not full, because the participant's task/evidence backing rides the stdio seam service, which is desktop-bound today: on web the participant degrades to conversation + view state while task operations and evidence verification wait for the remote seam.
rows.recoveryPath: Browser entrypoint + a seam transport port: the SeamClient stdio transport is one implementation of the seam; a remote transport (websocket to a server-side service instance) restores full task/evidence backing. core/service.mjs is already a standalone Node program.

rows.capability: Flauz service seam transport (stdio child-process spawn)
rows.reason: seamClient.ts spawns the zero-dep Node service (core/service.mjs) as a child process and speaks newline-delimited JSON over stdio. The web extension host has no child_process: the transport, not the service protocol, is the blocker. The human-gated terminal tool rides the same seam, so it shares this posture.
rows.recoveryPath: Transport port: keep core/service.mjs unchanged and add a remote transport (the service runs server-side or in a local desktop companion); the TL1-003 client-service seam is the designed integration point. No src/vs change needed.

rows.capability: evidence artifacts on local disk (artifacts module)
rows.reason: artifacts.ts writes evidence artifacts (hash chains, session marks) to local disk via node:fs/promises and hashes via node:crypto. The sinks are incidental, not architectural: the module is a writer behind the extension's activation, not a port-injected core.
rows.recoveryPath: Port the artifact sink onto vscode.workspace.fs (or the service-side store) and the hashing onto WebCrypto; the artifact formats are plain JSON files and stay unchanged.

rows.reason: main-only manifest (./dist/extension.js, no browser sibling): not-web under the same upstream isWebExtension() rule as every flauz-* extension today. The engine floor (^1.140.0) is host-neutral.
rows.recoveryPath: Browser entrypoint over the node-free core (policy engine + CDP transport + session manager); the workbench host adapter stays desktop-side.

rows.reason: policy.ts is node-free pure TypeScript: decisions are data-in/data-out over typed policy documents (deny sends zero CDP commands, fail-closed). A web extension host can run it unchanged; policy evaluation never touches the OS.
rows.recoveryPath: Packaging only: ship policy.ts from the browser entrypoint once one exists.

rows.reason: cdp/transport.ts speaks the STABLE global WebSocket (Node 22+ and every browser) with an injectable socket factory - zero runtime dependencies, no node: imports. The transport can attach to any reachable CDP endpoint from any host, which is exactly the stage-2 service shape.
rows.recoveryPath: Packaging only: the endpoint URL is configuration; a web build connects to a Flauz-controlled browser service endpoint instead of a local one.

rows.capability: browser runtime session manager, capture and journal sinks
rows.reason: The runtime core (session manager, recovery, tabs) is sound for web, but its sinks are local: session ids are minted with node:crypto randomBytes (runtime/session.ts), and screenshots/console/network captures plus the PIN-1 session journal are written via node:fs/promises (runtime/capture.ts, runtime/journal.ts). The blockers are the sinks and id minting, not the CDP conversation (see the transport row).
rows.recoveryPath: WebCrypto for session id minting; workspace.fs or service-backed sinks for captures and the journal. The session-manager state machine and the journal record format stay unchanged.

rows.capability: workbench browser host adapter (proposed browser API grant)
rows.reason: The WorkbenchBrowserHost adapter rides the proposed vscode.browser API (vendored vscode-dts/vscode.proposed.browser.d.ts; grant flauz.flauz-browser:["browser"]): an integrated browser page rendered as a workbench editor tab with a CDP session handle. That surface is desktop-workbench-bound in the current tree; the stage-2 architecture (ARCHITECTURE-LOCK section 3) runs the real browser as a Flauz-controlled sidecar, and on web the endpoint-host path is the designated route, not this adapter.
rows.recoveryPath: Not a web recovery: on web, browser surfaces go through the CdpEndpointHost path (node-free transport row) against a remote Flauz browser service. The workbench tab integration remains the desktop premium surface.

rows.reason: main-only manifest (./dist/extension.js, no browser sibling): not-web under the upstream isWebExtension() rule. The engine floor (^1.140.0) is host-neutral.
rows.recoveryPath: Browser entrypoint over the registry/lifecycle core; the local-real executor and its wiring stay desktop-side (their rows).

rows.capability: environment registry, descriptors, continuity and lifecycle core (port-injected)
rows.reason: The registry (registry.ts), the typed descriptor/continuity model (api.ts) and the whole lifecycle subtree (state machine, manager, executor port, store) are node-free: fs, spawn and hashing are injected ports wired from the extension host. The core can drive remote environment classes from a web host unchanged. Lead integration note (2026-09-28, TL1-005 merge): the production `NodeCliPort` (lifecycle/cliPort.ts, TL3-004 rung 1 — node:child_process) is a desktop-side injectable and sits deliberately OUTSIDE the node-free evidence set; the core + the CLI executors stay node-free by receiving the port (the injection law: web hosts ship the core with their own port implementation).
rows.recoveryPath: Packaging only: ship the core from the browser entrypoint; remote provider executors (TL3-004) plug into the same EnvironmentExecutor port.

rows.reason: The local-real executor spawns local processes as environments (fixed harness, SIGKILL escalation, real fs snapshots) and the extension wiring provides the spawn/hash/fs ports plus the .flauz persistence via node:fs/promises. The capability is local-process execution by definition: remote environment classes (SSH, container, cloud - TL3-004) are separate provider classes, not a web degradation of this one.
rows.recoveryPath: By design desktop: on web, environment execution goes through remote executors behind the same EnvironmentExecutor port. The lifecycle store/hashing wiring ports over (WebCrypto, workspace.fs) when the registry ships a browser entrypoint.

rows.reason: main-only manifest (./dist/extension.js, no browser sibling): not-web under the upstream isWebExtension() rule - and this extension has zero node imports, so for flauz-models the packaging posture is the ONLY blocker (see the capability row).
rows.recoveryPath: Add the browser entrypoint: the whole src tree is node-free, so the same code ships to both hosts (the cleanest first candidate for the Flauz web story).

rows.capability: multi-model provider seam, registry and mock provider
rows.reason: The entire src tree is node-free: provider descriptors, the registry and the languageModelChatProviders contribution (vendor flauz-mock) use only vscode API surfaces that exist on web. No local resource binding anywhere in the module.
rows.recoveryPath: Packaging only: a browser entrypoint makes the provider seam web-shipped; real provider adapters (TL2-002) must keep the node-free discipline or declare their own rows.

rows.reason: main-only manifest (./dist/extension.js, no browser sibling): not-web under the upstream isWebExtension() rule. The engine floor (^1.140.0) is host-neutral. Not in the work order six-extension list - the live tree carries this seventh extension from TL3-005, and the gate's glob-driven coverage rule demands classification for every flauz-* surface.
rows.recoveryPath: Add the browser entrypoint: the whole src tree is node-free, so the resource graph ships to both hosts from the same code.

rows.capability: logical resource graph (ResourceRef identity, typed edges, continuity plans, provenance ledger)
rows.reason: The entire src tree is node-free: ResourceRef identity, kind-specific access surfaces, typed edges, continuity/restoration plans and the resources-ops provenance ledger operate without any node: import. Vault-only secret refs are logical URNs, not local file access. On web the graph runs unchanged against the same .flauz/ state family.
rows.recoveryPath: Packaging only: a browser entrypoint makes the resource graph web-shipped alongside the workspace state it references.

rows.reason: main-only manifest (./dist/extension.js, no browser sibling): not-web under the upstream isWebExtension() rule. The engine floor (^1.140.0) is host-neutral.
rows.recoveryPath: Browser entrypoint over the envelope/messaging core; shell execution and the node crypto signer stay desktop-side (their rows).

rows.capability: workflow envelope, fragment validation and messaging core
rows.reason: envelope.ts (the WorkflowEnvelope contract, fragment validation, approval/tool ports) and messaging.ts are node-free: the envelope is data validation plus injected ports. Authoring, listing and validating workflows needs no OS access.
rows.recoveryPath: Packaging only: author/validate/list workflows from the browser entrypoint; execution stays desktop or moves behind a remote executor port.

rows.reason: The executor runs recorded command steps on the local shell in the workspace root via node:child_process (with node:os/fs for the working set). Local shell execution is the capability; the approval gate (QuickPickApprovalPort) is host-agnostic but the execution surface is not. A web form is a remote-brokered executor - a different ToolExecutorPort implementation, not a degradation.
rows.recoveryPath: By design desktop: web workflows dispatch steps to a remote executor behind the existing ToolExecutorPort (the port seam already exists); approval gates are already vscode.window-based.

rows.reason: keys.ts loads the checkpoint signer from node:crypto. The signature format and ledger discipline are portable; only the crypto provider is node-bound.
rows.recoveryPath: WebCrypto-backed CheckpointSigner port (the signer is already loaded behind a port boundary); signature verification shapes stay unchanged.

rows.reason: main-only manifest (./dist/extension.js, no browser sibling): not-web under the upstream isWebExtension() rule. The engine floor (^1.140.0) is host-neutral. This extension also owns the activity-bar shell (container flauz) - on web the whole Flauz shell is absent until this row recovers.
rows.recoveryPath: Browser entrypoint with a workspace.fs-backed FileSystemPort (the port seam exists in src/api.ts); the nodeFs wiring stays desktop-side.

rows.capability: task state + hash-chained evidence ledger services
rows.reason: taskService.ts and ledger.ts are node-free: the canonical .flauz/tasks.json state machine and the append-only hash-chained ledger operate entirely through the injected FileSystemPort (and injected hashing). On web the same services run against a workspace.fs port with unchanged on-disk formats.
rows.recoveryPath: Packaging plus one port implementation: a workspace.fs-backed FileSystemPort (the port is declared in src/api.ts) makes the services web-shipped with byte-identical state files.

rows.capability: workspace state wiring (nodeFs FileSystemPort + fsPath roots)
rows.reason: extension.ts wires the services to node:fs/promises and derives workspace roots from uri.fsPath. The port abstraction already exists - the nodeFs instance is the desktop wiring, and fsPath-rooted paths are meaningless against web virtual workspaces. The blocker is the wiring choice, not the services (see their row).
rows.recoveryPath: Implement the FileSystemPort over vscode.workspace.fs with Uri-relative joinPath in the browser build; the desktop entry keeps nodeFs. The port contract (src/api.ts) is shared, so no fork.

rows.reason: The provider module itself is node-free and the scmArtifactProvider grant is ingested host-agnostically, so the contribution parses on web. Degraded because artifact content retrieval is backed by the nodeFs wiring today: on web the provider serves workspace-fs-backed artifacts only, which is a subset of the desktop artifact surface until the port lands.
rows.recoveryPath: Same as the wiring row: the workspace.fs port restores the full artifact surface on web.
